sn9.9:1.1: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu, a Vajjian prince, was dwelling at Vesālī in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.9:1.2: Now on that occasion an all-night festival was being held in Vesālī.
sn9.9:1.3: Then that bhikkhu, lamenting as he heard the clamour of instruments, gongs, and music coming from Vesālī, on that occasion recited this verse:
sn9.9:2.1: “We dwell in the forest all alone
sn9.9:2.2: Like a log rejected in the woods.
sn9.9:2.3: On such a splendid night as this
sn9.9:2.4: Who is there worse off than us?”
sn9.9:3.1: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, having compassion for that bhikkhu, desiring his good, desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in him, approached him and addressed him in verse:
sn9.9:4.1: “As you dwell in the forest all alone
sn9.9:4.2: Like a log rejected in the woods,
sn9.9:4.3: Many are those who envy you,
sn9.9:4.4: As hell-beings envy those going to heaven.”
sn9.9:5.1: Then that bhikkhu, stirred up by that devatā, acquired a sense of urgency.
